_meta.interpretation: Very strongly. The correlation sits close to its ceiling and its interval is narrow, so spending during the test follows earlier spending along an almost perfect straight line: customers who spent more before spend more now. A correlation this high says the two measures rise and fall together; on its own it says nothing about cause, and nothing about whether spending went up overall, which is a before-and-after comparison of the same customers.
_meta.question: Do customers who spent more before the test also spend more during it?
_meta.description: Pearson r between post-treatment revenue and the pre-treatment baseline, computed streaming via an extended Welford recurrence.
_meta.name: pearson_correlation
